column3: Identify a concrete pleasant aspect of the wait or meal, such as conversation or enjoying food. Complaining alone or merely promising punctuality does not meet the mission.
column4: 기다리는 동안 같이 온 사람과 여유롭게 이야기할 수 있었어.
column5: The wait gave us time to chat without rushing.
column6: 待つ間に、一緒に来た人とゆっくり話せた。

column3: Identify enjoyment or connection at the board-game gathering despite losing. A promise to win next time alone is insufficient.
column4: 승패와 별개로 친구들과 웃으며 시간을 보낸 게 좋았어.
column5: Even without winning, laughing with my friends was fun.
column6: 勝てなくても、友達と笑って過ごせたのが楽しかった。

column3: Find a real benefit of sleeping longer, such as rest or restored energy, without denying that cleaning was delayed.
column4: 청소는 늦어졌지만 몸이 필요했던 잠을 푹 잤어.

column3: Find a benefit of cooking instead of ordering delivery, such as choosing ingredients, saving money, or practicing cooking.

column6: 材料を自分で選び、好みの味にできた。

column3: Identify why rain starting near home was fortunate, such as being able to get an umbrella before getting far away.
column4: 멀리 나가기 전에 비가 와서 우산을 챙길 수 있어 다행이야.
column5: Luckily, the rain started while I could still go back for an umbrella.
column6: 遠くへ行く前に雨が降ったから、傘を取りに戻れてよかった。

column3: Recognize that autosave preserved most of the report despite losing ten lines. An apology or generic reassurance alone is insufficient.
column4: 자동 저장 덕분에 처음부터 다시 쓰지 않아도 돼서 다행이야.
column5: Luckily, autosave means I don't have to start the whole report again.
column6: 自動保存のおかげで、最初から書き直さずに済んでよかった。

column3: Recognize noticing the ankle signal early or avoiding further strain by stopping. Do not require a medical claim or deny the discomfort.
column4: 무리하기 전에 몸의 신호를 알아차리고 멈춰서 다행이야.
column5: I'm glad I noticed the discomfort and stopped before pushing further.
column6: 無理をする前に体の違和感に気づいて、やめられてよかった。

column3: Name a plausible new opportunity or activity because the usual cafe is closed. Generic reassurance without an opportunity is insufficient.
column4: 이번 기회에 골목의 새로운 카페를 가봐야겠어.
column5: This is a chance to try a new café nearby.
column6: この機会に、近くの新しいカフェへ行ってみよう。

column3: Suggest a feasible enjoyable use of the hour before the movie. Merely blaming oneself or promising to check times next time is insufficient.

column5: I can take a walk nearby and enjoy the evening scenery.
column6: 一時間、近くを散歩して夕方の景色を楽しもう。

column3: Find a learning or exploration opportunity in taking an unfamiliar history class instead of the preferred elective.

column5: This is a chance to discover an interest in a new area of history.
column6: 知らなかった歴史を学び、新しい興味を見つける機会だ。

column3: Identify a realistic upside of the shorter haircut, such as a new style, easier care, or comfort. Accept disappointment; do not require pretending to like everything.
column4: 아직 낯설지만 머리를 말리고 손질하는 시간이 줄겠어.
column5: It feels unfamiliar, but drying and styling it will take less time.
column6: まだ慣れないけれど、乾かしたり整えたりする時間は短くなりそう。

column3: Reframe comparison in guitar learning through one's own pace, enjoyment, progress, or learning from a peer without belittling either person.
column4: 내 속도로 음악을 즐기면서 잘하는 사람에게 배울 수도 있겠어.
column5: I can enjoy music at my own pace and learn from someone more experienced.
column6: 自分のペースで音楽を楽しみながら、上手な人から学ぶこともできる。

column3: Find a real benefit or feasible alternative after the ferry cancellation, such as safety or a different Jeju activity. Acknowledge disappointment without claiming the trip is ruined.
column4: 아쉽지만 안전하게 남은 제주 동네를 더 둘러볼 수 있겠어.
column5: It's disappointing, but I can safely explore another part of Jeju.
column6: 残念だけれど、安全に済州島の別の場所を見て回れそう。

column3: Find a benefit or constructive next step in meeting unfamiliar coworkers, such as making connections or learning about another team.
column4: 다른 부서 사람들을 알아가고 새로운 이야기를 들을 기회였어.
column5: It was a chance to meet coworkers and hear new perspectives.
column6: 他部署の人を知り、新しい話を聞く機会になった。

column3: Identify a meaningful aspect of family-event spending or a feasible next budgeting step, without dismissing the savings goal or blaming others.
column4: 저축은 덜 했지만 소중한 사람들을 챙겼고, 다음 달엔 경조사 예산을 따로 잡아볼래.
column5: I saved less, but cared for people who matter; next month I'll budget for these events.
column6: 貯金は少なかったけれど、大切な人を気遣えた。来月は行事の予算も作ろう。

column3: Find learning, effort, a reusable piece of work, or a concrete constructive next step after contest rejection. Merely insulting judges or claiming failure proves worthlessness fails.
column4: 결과는 아쉽지만 작품을 완성한 경험을 다음 작업에 살릴 수 있어.
column5: The result hurts, but I can use the experience of finishing a piece in my next project.
column6: 結果は残念だけれど、作品を完成させた経験を次に生かせる。

column3: Find learning, progress, or a feasible next step after repeated job rejections, without guaranteeing success or blaming oneself or recruiters globally.
column4: 이번 지원 경험을 바탕으로 이력서를 다듬고 더 맞는 공고를 찾아볼래.
column5: I can use what I've learned to improve my résumé and look for roles that fit better.
column6: 今回の経験をもとに履歴書を見直し、より合う求人を探してみよう。

column3: Separate a coworker's curt behavior from one's own worth or total responsibility. Accept uncertainty about their motives. Blaming oneself entirely or attacking the coworker's character fails.
column4: 필요한 질문을 한 건 잘못이 아니고, 상대의 기분까지 내가 책임질 필요는 없어.
column5: Asking a necessary question wasn't wrong, and their mood isn't all my responsibility.
column6: 必要な質問をしたことは悪くないし、相手の気分まで自分が背負わなくていい。

column3: Judge the job choice using the information available at the time; acknowledge uncertainty rather than condemning one's past self. A plan alone without this perspective is insufficient.
column4: 입사 전에는 알기 어려운 부분도 있었어. 그때 신중히 고른 나를 탓하지 말자.
column5: Some things were hard to know before joining. I made a careful choice with what I knew.
column6: 入社前には分からないこともあった。そのとき慎重に選んだ自分を責めなくていい。

column3: Acknowledge forgetting the birthday without equating that mistake with being a bad or selfish person. A sincere repair action may support the answer, but attacking the friend fails.
column4: 생일을 놓친 건 미안하지만 그 실수 하나로 내가 나쁜 친구가 되는 건 아니야.
column5: I'm sorry I missed the birthday, but one mistake doesn't make me a bad friend.
column6: 誕生日を忘れたことは申し訳ないけれど、一度のミスで悪い友達になるわけではない。

column3: Respond kindly to fatigue and the limited study session rather than equating tiredness with laziness or worthlessness. Accept rest, bodily limits, or acknowledging effort.
column4: 피곤한 몸으로 공부하러 간 것도 노력한 거야. 오늘은 쉬어도 괜찮아.
column5: Going there while tired was an effort too. It's okay to rest today.
column6: 疲れていても勉強に行ったのは頑張ったこと。今日は休んでも大丈夫。

column3: Separate a relative's intrusive remarks from one's value and life choices. Allow boundaries and different timelines; do not blame oneself or insult the relative's entire character.
column4: 상대의 무례한 말이 내 가치를 정하지 않아. 내 삶은 내 속도로 살아도 돼.
column5: Their rude remarks don't define my worth. I can live at my own pace.
column6: 相手の無礼な言葉で自分の価値は決まらない。自分のペースで生きていい。

column3: Recognize the twenty days of journaling as meaningful effort rather than treating ten missed days as total failure. A future plan alone without recognizing existing effort is insufficient.
column4: 빈 날도 있지만 스무 날이나 기록한 노력은 사라지지 않아.
column5: The blank days don't erase the effort of writing on twenty days.
column6: 空白の日があっても、二十日も書いた努力は消えない。

column3: Recognize reading half the book as partial progress and accept attention limits without global self-criticism.
column4: 절반을 읽은 것도 배움이야. 쉬었다가 내 속도로 이어가면 돼.
column5: Reading half was learning too. I can rest and continue at my own pace.
column6: 半分読んだことも学びだ。休んでから、自分のペースで続ければいい。

column3: Treat losing an earbud as an unfortunate mistake rather than proof of a defective identity. Accept sadness or practical next steps without self-abuse.
column4: 잃어버려서 속상하지만 물건 하나 잃었다고 내가 못난 사람인 건 아니야.
column5: I'm upset about losing it, but one lost item doesn't make me a bad person.
column6: なくして悲しいけれど、物を一つなくしたからといって、だめな人間ではない。

column3: Acknowledge effort, perseverance, or partial achievements over the year rather than judging the entire year or self as worthless because some goals were missed.
column4: 다 이루지는 못했지만 한 해를 살아내며 애쓴 나의 노력은 의미 있어.
column5: I didn't do everything, but the effort I put into getting through this year matters.
column6: 全部はできなかったけれど、この一年を生きて頑張った努力には意味がある。
